title: Public Relations: An Introduction
summary: Public relations (PR) is a two-way communication process between an organisation and its public, aimed at changing the public's mindset in a certain direction; it is a form of communication used to persuade or influence people by ethical means. Communication and PR are linked. Communication in PR is a receiver-controlled phenomenon (a speech in Hindi to an audience that does not understand Hindi is no communication), so the key is to focus on the 'key public' (hospitals – patients, merchants – customers, schools – students, television – viewers, radio – listeners). PR wins the support of the public by addressing their wants, interests and needs. Road sign boards are a simple example. The communication has three progressive levels: Awareness (the message reaches the public), Acceptance (the public agrees) and Action (the public acts). PR is the result of what you do, what you say and what others say about you. The main aim of PR is to build goodwill.

Ancient examples: kings going in disguise to learn what people felt (Sultan Haroon-Al-Rashid), bards singing the glory of kings, Bhadro reporting popular feeling to Rama in the Ramayana; King Ashoka sent his children to Sri Lanka to spread Buddhism, and his daughter Sanghamitra was the first woman PR executive; religious teachers (Buddha, Shankaracharya, Nanak, Kabir) and Mahatma Gandhi were master communicators. Systematic PR practice began with the Indian Railways in the 1920s (exhibitions, festivals, ads in newspapers in India and England to attract tourists).

The Central Publicity Board set up during the First World War (1914–18) was the first organised PR set-up of the Government of India (later Central Bureau of Information and then Bureau of Public Information); feedback was one of its tasks. After 1947 the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (sectors: information, broadcasting, film) was set up. Its media units: All India Radio (radio), Doordarshan Kendra (television), Films Division (film), Press Information Bureau (print), Registrar of Newspapers for India (print), National Film Archives of India (film), Photo Division (photographs), Indian Institute of Mass Communication, Film and Television Institute of India, National Film Development Corporation (films), National Centre of Films for Children and Young Persons, Directorate of Film Festivals, Publications Division (print), Directorate of Field Publicity (film, outdoor media), Directorate of Advertising and Visual Publicity – DAVP (print, radio, TV, outdoor, exhibitions), Song and Drama Division (drama, folk songs, ballets), Research and Reference Division. PIB gives official information to the press through press releases; its head, the Principal Information Officer, is the official spokesperson. DAVP is responsible for all media publicity and campaigns for the Central Government and releases ads to newspapers, magazines, radio and TV. Photo Division supplies official photographs. Field Publicity Unit organises exhibitions and melas. Song and Drama Division uses music, drama and folk media. Films Division makes publicity films and newsreels. The Research and Reference Wing supports ministries. The Ministry of External Affairs has the XP Division for media and publicity. Each state has a Directorate of Information and Public Relations with Field Publicity Officers.

Purposes: educate audiences on the advantages of a product, promote goodwill for the organisation, and create, maintain and protect its reputation. Product PR: launching or promoting products by awareness and differentiation, giving samples or discounts, special events, exhibitions, window display, media events such as press conferences and printed material (pamphlets, brochures). Employee relations: earning the goodwill of employees through newsletters, bulletin boards, picnics, incentives and opportunities for education. Government and political relations: campaigns, public meetings, posters, hoardings and schemes (public distribution system) to win votes. Community relations: banks, business houses and media organisations maintain parks, run clean-up and beautification drives, set up charitable dispensaries, sponsor cricket matches, set up public libraries and raise funds in natural calamities.

vsa: List any three purposes of Public Relations.
To educate audiences on the advantages of a product; to promote goodwill for the organisation; to create, maintain and protect the organisation's reputation.
List any four media units under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.
AIR, Doordarshan Kendra, Films Division, Press Information Bureau (also DAVP, Photo Division).
Describe the functions of PIB and DAVP.
PIB issues official press releases to the media; DAVP handles publicity campaigns and advertising for central ministries.
A form of communication used to persuade or influence people by ethical means through two-way communication between an organisation and its public.
What is the role of the Song and Drama Division?
It uses music, drama and folk media to publicise government programmes through performing artists.
sa: Define public relations and explain its importance.
PR is a two-way ethical communication to persuade the public; it builds goodwill, educates about products and policies, creates and protects reputation and wins public support.
Describe the functions of any two government media units that help in communicating policies to the public.
PIB issues press releases to print media; DAVP releases advertisements and runs publicity campaigns; Song and Drama Division uses folk media.
Explain product PR and employee relations.
Product PR launches products through samples, events, exhibitions and window display; employee relations earn goodwill through newsletters, bulletin boards, picnics and incentives.
Organisations gain community goodwill through parks, clean-up drives, charitable dispensaries, sponsorships, public libraries and fund-raising in calamities.
la: Describe the structure of government public relations in India.

The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (information, broadcasting, film) has media units such as AIR, DDK, PIB, DAVP, Films Division, Photo Division and Song and Drama Division; states have Directorates of Information and Public Relations.
Explain the types of public relations.
Product PR, employee relations, government and political relations and community relations, each with its methods.
